title: Notion Linear Integration: How to Connect Them (2026)
summary: Notion Linear integration watches one app for changes and writes updates to the other through Activepieces, handling data sync automatically.
body_markdown:
## Five Notion and Linear workflows you can build in Activepieces


Nobody has to be hired to cover most Notion and Linear traffic with five small workflows.


You describe the process to the built-in chat in[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) , say "when a Linear issue is updated, change the matching Notion row", and it builds and publishes a real workflow you can read, version and approve.


That flow sits under the same RBAC and audit logs as every other flow on the platform, and each run leaves a trace anyone can read, no certification needed. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


The shape of the two integrations decides where each one starts, so starting points can't be arbitrary.


Count the steps and the split is clear: Notion offers 4 triggers and 15 actions, and Linear offers 8 triggers and 13 actions, per the[Activepieces pieces API](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) .


Notion's therefore better at receiving writes than at starting a workflow, and Linear's the reverse. The table pairs each workflow with the app that fires it.


Workflow Trigger and app Actions and app Work saved


Page to issue "New Database Item" (Notion) "Create Issue" (Linear) Retyping a request into the tracker


Issue to row Linear issue-created trigger (Linear) "Create Database Item" (Notion) Hand-copying new issues into a planning database


Status sync "Updated Issue" (Linear) "Update Database Item" (Notion) Chasing status in two places


Digest "Updated Issue" (Linear) "Create Page" (Notion) Assembling release notes from memory


AI summary "Updated Page" (Notion) An AI step, then "Create Issue" (Linear) Writing the issue title and body


*Prices and plan limits checked against[activepieces.com](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/notion) and[activepieces.com](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/linear) on November 15, 2026.*


Take one row at a time: build that workflow and test it on one record before you build the next. Notion's step names are from[its piece page](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/notion) .


Start with "New Database Item" in Notion and map its fields into "Create Issue" in Linear. Test with one row. If the issue lands with the wrong team or an empty description, the mapping is wrong, and you find that before anyone else does.


Run it the other way when Linear is where work begins. Linear's issue-created trigger feeds Notion's "Create Database Item". Because Linear has 8 triggers, you have room to filter on one of them rather than sending every event into Notion.


### Status sync between the two


Build this one first: "Updated Issue" in Linear into "Update Database Item" in Notion.


Going back the other way starts from Notion's "Updated Database Item", but I can't point to a Linear update step in the findings.


Use an HTTP request to Linear's API there. Keep it as a separate workflow so two updates can't trigger each other in a loop.


Let "Updated Issue" write finished work into a Notion page with "Create Page", then filter that database by week. The digest's a view, not a workflow, so there's less to break. The only thing you still write by hand's the editorial line on top.


### Optional AI step: summarise before filing


Put an AI step between Notion's "Updated Page" and Linear's "Create Issue" to turn a long page into a short title and description. Test this one last, because it's the only step whose output changes on each run.


With the five workflows laid out, the next question is how far each integration's trigger and action counts will carry them.
